newsitem.title: USA: Blue Cross of Minn. to proceed with tobacco suit.
newsitem.headline: Blue Cross of Minn. to proceed with tobacco suit.

text.p: Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Minnesota said Friday it plans to proceed with its lawsuit against the tobacco industry despite a settlement with the states.
The non-profit health service plan corporation said its suit, which seeks to recoup benefits paid on behalf of subscribers, will not be dismissed because of the settlement.

On Friday, tobacco companies agreed to pay $368.5 billion, admit that tobacco is addictive and accept extensive federal regulation over their products and advertising as part of the landmark agreement with states.
Blue Cross and Blue Shield, however, said the agreement does not appear to dismiss private lawsuits such as the one it has filed.
"Our litigation is not settled by the announced deal," Andy Czajkowski, president and chief executive of Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Minnesota, said in a statement.
In addition, he said the settlement does not accomplish what the corporation set out to do with its suit, "Namely, to fundamentally change the way the tobacco industry does business."
In return for the settlement, tobacco companies would be given immunity from any further punitive liability for deception, fraud or conspiracy that might have occurred in the past.

"While details of the settlement agreement are just now coming to light, we urge Congress and the White House not to give in to any deal that contributes more to tobacco's interests than to the health interests of Minnesotans and all Americans," Czajkowski said.
